A Bloomberg report yesterday pointed out that future Apple Watch lineups could see considerable changes.

The report specifically mentioned that Apple is exploring the launch of one or more models featuring a round face rather than a square one……

Most smartwatches are round

Although square-faced watches have existed for over a century, traditional watches are mostly round, and the same goes for Android smartwatches. Examples include:

  • Amazfit Active Max
  • Samsung Galaxy Watch 9
  • Motorola Moto Watch
  • All Garmin models (Venu, Epix Pro, Forerunner, Fenix)
  • Google Pixel Watch

Apple's choice of a rectangular design is an outlier, so it would not be surprising for the company to consider launching a round Apple Watch in the future.

Arguments in favour of a round Apple Watch

The reason Apple originally chose a rectangular design was to display more information. The other screens we use daily — phones, tablets, laptops, monitors and so on — are all rectangular, and that is no coincidence.

Ultimately, this trade-off is really a question of aesthetics versus practicality. Some people will always put practicality first, so the rectangular Apple Watch will definitely not disappear. But there are also many people who place great importance on appearance, and whether it's a traditional watch or a smartwatch, many people have a strong preference for a round face.

Besides, not everyone who wears an Apple Watch needs to see a lot of information on the screen. There are actually many reasons to wear an Apple Watch, even if you hardly ever look at the screen. For example:

  • Health and fitness monitoring
  • Sleep tracking
  • Emergency features, such as fall detection
  • Contactless payment

For many people, the first item is the biggest selling point. If you mainly don't use your Apple Watch to view content, then a round screen is absolutely sufficient for you.

But the case for an Apple Ring is even stronger

However, if you belong to this category of user — primarily using an Apple Watch for health and fitness monitoring and not really using it to view information — I would say a smart ring is the wiser choice.

I personally switched from an Apple Watch to an Oura smart ring back in 2024, and have just upgraded to the fifth generation. I love how understated it is, that I can wear a traditional watch of my own choice, and that it only needs charging once a week.

Almost two years ago I said that I had already been completely won over by the smart ring as an Apple Watch alternative, and thought Apple should launch one. To this day I still firmly believe this, and Gurman says Eddy Cue is also very fond of smart rings, which shows the chances of one being launched are actually quite high.

I do think it's possible Apple will launch a round Apple Watch, but I believe even more strongly that we'll see an Apple Ring. What do you think? Feel free to share your views in the comments.
